Culcasi (1991) 229 CA3d 209, 220, 280 CR 766, 772 (emphasis in original); see also Chatton v. National Union Fire Ins. Co. of Pittsburgh, Penn. (1992) 10 CA4th 846, 854, 13 CR2d 318, 323—“bodily injury” does not include nonphysical, emotional or mental harm] (2) [3:357] No accidental “occurrence”: More fundamentally, CGL bodily injury coverage requires an “occurrence,” which is defined as an “accident.” [CG 00 01 12 07, Sec. V, ¶ 13] Employment termination by nature is an intentional act. It is not an accidental “occurrence” even if the employee suffers injuries not intended by the employer. [Dyer v. Northbrook Property & Cas. Ins. Co. (1989) 210 CA3d 1540, 1547-1548, 259 CR 298, 303—no coverage for emotional distress arising from employment termination; B & E Convalescent Ctr. v. State Comp. Ins.
